newsitem.title: KENYA: Uganda, U.S. to hold coffee tasting via Internet.
newsitem.headline: Uganda, U.S. to hold coffee tasting via Internet.

text.p: Coffee tasters in Uganda and the United States will hold their first Internet coffee tasting next week in what is being hailed as a direct dialogue between consumers and growers, a Ugandan trade group said on Thursday.

"The first Internet coffee tasting on September 17 opens a direct dialogue between growers and consumers. Though half a world apart, tasters will be able to critique identical coffee and see each other's reactions via a "CU-seeme' Internet video connection," the private Uganda Coffee Trade Federation said.

"Tasters will exchange written comments. If Internet bandwidth allows, each site will be able to hear the unique sounds of coffee cup tasting or "cupping' at the other site," the Federation added in a statement.

It said a panel of experienced coffee tasters at each site would taste the same two coffees, both premium Ugandan arabica coffees - Bugisu AA and Bugisu Peaberry. The coffees have been checked by speciality roaster Quartermaine's Coffee.

"Over cups of coffee that are half a world away, yet identically prepared, growers and consumers will be able to share comments about the coffee and concerns about how it was produced," the Federation said.

The Federation's membership of 50 includes coffee growers, traders, exporters, bankers, insurers and transporters. It professes "commitment to quality coffee from farms and factories that respect the environment and are socially responsible".
The Federation said the tasting would begin a programme to put consumers and producers in a direct dialogue using the Internet, which became widely available in Uganda this year.

Federation chairman Paul Mugambwa, himself a coffee grower, said, "We don't have the advertising budget of countries like Colombia so we are looking...to cost-effective ways of telling people about Ugandan coffee."
He added, "For example, one of the federation's ideas is to support a "women's coffee', grown by women farmers and processed by factories that women own and operate."

Federation Executive Director Fred Kawuma said Ugandans sought a global level playing field that would allow them leap over international middlemen to capture more of their coffee's world market value.

"We want to base the growth of Uganda coffee in the U.S. on trust -- trust in quality and trust in our farmers and the way they grow coffee," Kawuma added, but did not say what proportion of Uganda coffee exports go to the United States.
Uganda is Africa's leading coffee producer. --Nairobi Newsroom ++254-2 330-261.
